gen_risks.description: Inadequate capacity of training institutions to deliver high-quality, market-relevant training may hinder project effectiveness.
gen_risks.mitigation: Provide targeted support to training institutions, including equipment, curricula development, and instructor upskilling.
gen_risks.evidence: Component 1: Institutional Foundations for More and Better Jobs

gen_risks.description: Insufficient private sector engagement and demand for skilled workers may limit the effectiveness of training programs.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish workforce development committees to review training offerings and identify skills gaps, and provide just-in-time technical trainings aligned with private sector needs.
gen_risks.evidence: Component 1: Institutional Foundations for More and Better Jobs

gen_risks.description: Limited access to finance and lack of entrepreneurial skills may hinder the growth and sustainability of MSMEs.
gen_risks.mitigation: Provide business management training, hands-on mentoring, and access to finance opportunities to selected MSMEs.
gen_risks.evidence: Component 2: Pathways to More and Better Jobs

gen_risks.description: Climate-related hazards, such as floods and droughts, may disrupt project implementation and affect the livelihoods of beneficiaries.
gen_risks.mitigation: Incorporate climate considerations into project design and implementation, and provide support for climate-resilient infrastructure investments.

gen_risks.description: Inequitable distribution of project benefits may exacerbate existing social and economic inequalities.
gen_risks.mitigation: Apply gender-responsive enrollment targets, ensure accessible training locations, and provide childcare support where feasible.
gen_risks.evidence: Component 1: Institutional Foundations for More and Better Jobs

gen_risks.description: Inadequate monitoring and evaluation may hinder the project's ability to track progress and make data-driven decisions.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish a robust monitoring and evaluation system, including regular data collection and analysis.

gen_risks.description: Delays in project implementation may impact the achievement of project objectives and the realization of benefits.
gen_risks.mitigation: Develop a detailed project schedule, establish a coordination committee, and provide regular progress updates.

gen_risks.description: Insufficient funding or changes in funding arrangements may impact project implementation and sustainability.
gen_risks.mitigation: Develop a comprehensive financial management plan, including budgeting, procurement, and disbursement arrangements.

gen_risks.description: Inadequate governance and institutional arrangements may hinder project implementation and coordination.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish clear roles and responsibilities, ensure effective communication and coordination among stakeholders, and provide capacity-building support to institutions.

gen_risks.description: Risks of exclusion, elite capture, and community health and safety risks may arise if project benefits are not equitably distributed or if barriers to participation persist.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement measures to promote inclusivity, ensure accessible training locations, and provide support for vulnerable groups.

gt_risks.description: Frequent government changes and the cross-ministerial nature of the jobs agenda can shift policy direction, counterpart arrangements, and implementation momentum; further changes may follow the mid-2026 legislative/parliamentary elections. Success depends on sustained coordination across labor, education, tourism, agriculture, and finance ministries plus private-sector engagement.
gt_risks.mitigation: Anchor the project within MLSSS (core employment-promotion mandate); strengthen technical ownership at directorate level rather than relying on political leadership; establish a formal coordination committee and a unified PIU; continue policy dialogue with Government during implementation.

gt_risks.description: STP's fragile growth outlook, narrow fiscal space, and dependence on external financing leave it highly vulnerable to external shocks (energy/food price swings, donor-disbursement delays, climate events), which may weaken labor demand, reduce firms' absorption capacity, and constrain the Government's ability to sustain recurrent-cost interventions (training, stipends, employment services).
gt_risks.mitigation: Prioritize low-cost, scalable interventions; combine supply-side investments with direct job-creation support; target sectors with growth potential and external demand linkages (incl. labor mobility); coordinate with other World Bank macro-fiscal/energy/private-sector engagements in STP.

gt_risks.description: Limited experience of MLSSS and DTEFP in delivering complex labor-market interventions at scale; fragmented institutional landscape; multiple implementation partners; nascent capacity in labor-market analytics, employment intermediation, and cross-sectoral coordination; sustainability risk if new systems/programs are not institutionalized within government structures and budgets.
gt_risks.mitigation: Leverage existing institutions/mechanisms rather than parallel structures (existing MLSSS PIU, coordination committee, AFAP for fiduciary/safeguards); finance targeted TA and staffing; invest in durable institutional assets (labor-market information system, employability portal, strengthened training institutions, formalized service-provider arrangements); use the learning agenda and impact evaluation to identify cost-effective interventions for scale-up.

gt_risks.description: Complex procurement in a small-island context: residual FM risk is moderate but residual procurement risk is substantial, driven by the complexity of civil works in a remote island context, the large number of technical-assistance contracts, and the multiplicity of projects already handled by AFAP.
gt_risks.mitigation: Agree ToRs and technical specifications between AFAP and the World Bank before initiating any procurement (prior and post-review); reinforce AFAP procurement and contract-management capacity incl. specialized support for civil-works supervision; embed dedicated fiduciary controls for the grants/stipends payment mechanism in the Project Operations Manual; continue and adapt the risk assessment during implementation.
